title: Explaining Opus
description:
Using a model without the reasoning capacity to hold every moving part in context simultaneously is what causes automation projects to collapse mid-build.

Opus handles the level of complexity that comes with designing multi-component systems. Mapping how an automation's parts connect, anticipating where the logic branches, working through failures in real time without losing track of earlier decisions, all of that requires a model that can hold more architecture in context than Sonnet or Haiku can sustain. The ceiling on simpler models shows up exactly when the system gets complicated enough to matter.

The cost resolves once you account for when the build happens. You build the automation once and it runs from that point. Spending more at the stage that determines whether the whole architecture holds is the only place in the process where the model cost is directly proportional to the long-term output quality.
